newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KPN KEEN TO GET ON WITH INTEGRATING TNT.
newsitem.headline: KPN KEEN TO GET ON WITH INTEGRATING TNT.

text.p: The postal unit of Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said on Friday it was keen to get on with the task of integrating Australian transport firm TNT Ltd into its own structure.
KPN earlier said it was entitled to 56 percent of TNT's issued ordinary shares and declared its offer unconditional.

"We want such a shareholding so we can manage TNT properly, so we're aiming for a 90 percent share in the firm, then we have to look and see which of our activities coincide and where integration is applicable," said PTT Post head Ad Scheepbouwer.
KPN was forced to wait to gain control during its 2.7 billion guilder bid for TNT before Bankers Trust of Australia finally put a blocking 19.9 percent stake into its offer.

Scheepbouwer said the road appeared clear towards KPN's goal of complete control of TNT. "Now that we're over 50 percent and Bankers Trust have tendered their shares that will take a big obstacle away," he said in a telephone interview.

"Until yesterday, we were a bidder, now we're the majority shareholder and we have to look at more detailed information -- until now not available to us -- and to see which of those businesses fit within our focus," he said.
Scheepbouwer said it was too early to say which businesses would be sold off during the integration or discuss the scale of any potential job losses.

"No doubt there will be some businesses that don't (fit in the new structure), no doubt we will find other solutions for those businesses. At the moment there's probably more of those businesses outside Europe than inside," he said.

"What we are planning is to integrate a number of businesses, it could happen that we have two depots in the same street, so that could mean job losses at some of the companies where we integrate," he said.
He said the immediate job in hand would be to integrate in those areas where there was most duplication of activities -- the Netherlands, Australia, Italy, Germany and Britain.
"Once we are an integrated company, which has its absolute strength in Europe, Asia and the Middle East, that's when we will capitalise on our economies of scale and gain more market share," he said.

Scheepbouwer said KPN saw future growth from the postal division expanding faster in international activities than in domestic business as postal business in the Netherlands would feel the pinch from electronic communications.
In October, when KPN announced its A$2.45 per share offer for TNT, Scheepbouwer said KPN saw annual postal revenues rising to 13 billion guilders from the six billion currently.
He saw revenue rising to six billion in the Netherlands and seven billion from the rest of the world compared to the current five billion guilders and one billion respectively.

"I think the activities outside the Netherlands will grow faster than those inside the Netherlands because in the letter traffic there's a lot of substitutions from electronic means." Scheepbouwer said on Friday.
Scheepbouwer said he did not think it a priority for PTT Post to make further purchases as the company had achieved the position it wanted in Europe.

"What we have to do is down the road make up our minds what our position will be in the United States. Will it be in a service network, an alliance, or do we have to make an acquisition there?" he said.

"Our focus is on domestic and international express, on logistics and on international mail, and with that focus we've got our work laid out for us for the next few years." -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 504 5000
